text: Track 5.1 On today's show, we're going to talk about veganism. Vegan's, for those who don't know, are people who choose not to eat or use any animal products. It seems that more and more people are going vegan because it's healthy and possibly fashionable. There is no doubt that the number of people reducing the animal products they eat, whether it's meat, cheese or eggs, has gone up in the past few years. The number of vegans in the UK, for example, increased by 360% between 2006 and 2018. But is it good for you? Let's try and find out. With me is Clark Martin, a successful food blogger who is also a vegan. Should I become a vegan, Clark? Well, what do you think? Should you keep eating meat and destroy your body and the planet at the same time? It's common knowledge that veganism has a lot of health benefits. We eat a lot of fruit, vegetables, nuts and seeds as part of our diet, and stay away from fats, eggs and milk products, which increase the risk of heart disease and certain types of cancer. There is no question that being a vegan is better for you. Well, researchers would agree with you. There are studies showing that vegans are less likely to be overweight and have heart disease. I've also read somewhere that veganism reduces stress, not sure if that's true. However, one of the issues with being vegan is that you don't get all the vitamins that you need, especially vitamin B12, which helps make blood and keeps the brain healthy. Everyone knows that vitamin B12 is common in meat, fish and eggs, but not in plants. Well, that's just fantastic. I can't get B12. Most people think that we all have vitamin problems, but again, this is just not true. We get most of our vitamins from the foodweed, but we also take tablets. The problem is that many people go vegan and think, okay, now I'm much healthier. But before you go vegan, you need to do a bit of research into what food groups you should eat and how often. Speaking of studies, here's another one that says vegans have a lower risk of heart disease, but a higher risk of other serious diseases. It also says that vegans have a higher risk of breaking their bones. What do you think about that? All vegans are weak, right? Listen, studies compare us with meat eaters and look for differences. It's a fact that vegans are in better health, but there may be other health differences that have nothing to do with the diet. All I'm saying is that going vegan makes you feel better. I have more energy and my concentration and performance have improved a lot. Why don't you learn a few recipes and try it for yourself? Maybe I'll do that. I'll get myself some.
